void NativeDynamicShapePlan::setGraphExecutionMode(GraphExecutionMode mode) {
  DSP_REQUIRE_PLAN_PHASE_AT_MOST(PlanPhase::SLOT_BY_SLOT, "setGraphExecutionMode");
  DSP_DIAG(EXECUTE, "setGraphExecutionMode: %d -> %d", static_cast<int>(graphExecutionMode_), static_cast<int>(mode));
  graphExecutionMode_ = mode;
  // Reset cached backends so mode changes take effect immediately.
  gpuGraphBackendChecked_ = false;
  gpuGraphBackend_ = nullptr;
  cpuGraphBackendChecked_ = false;
  cpuGraphBackend_ = nullptr;
  cpuGraphBackendChainBuilt_ = false;
  cpuGraphBackendChain_.clear();
  // Enable GPU graph capture for all modes except SLOT_BY_SLOT.
  // JIT backends (Triton/NVRTC/PTX) use graph capture when they
  // can't handle a segment (unsupported ops, etc).
  if (mode != GraphExecutionMode::GEM_SLOT_BY_SLOT) {
    gpuGraphCaptureEnabled_ = true;
  }
  // Clear GPU backend failed-compilation cache so segments that failed with
  // incomplete shapes (e.g., attention with seqK=0 before KV setup)
  // can retry when called again with correct external input shapes.
  clearGpuBackendFailedCache();
}

/**
 * Autoregressive decode loop with static KV cache for CUDA graph capture.
 *
 * <p>Encapsulates the full decode pipeline: prefill with dynamic KV, transition to
 * fixed-shape static KV buffers, frozen shapes for CUDA graph replay, GPU-side
 * token sampling via {@link TokenSample}, and per-step KV scatter.</p>
 *
 * <p>Usage:</p>
 * <pre>{@code
 * StaticKvCacheDecodeLoop loop = StaticKvCacheDecodeLoop.builder()
 *     .decoder(decoder)
 *     .embedTokens(embedTokens)
 *     .tokenizer(tokenizer)
 *     .maxNewTokens(256)
 *     .hiddenSize(hiddenSize)
 *     .build();
 * GenerationResult result = loop.decode(prefillEmbeddings, promptTokenIds);
 * }</pre>
 */
@Slf4j
@Builder
public class StaticKvCacheDecodeLoop {

    private static final int DEFAULT_DIAGNOSTIC_STEPS = 3;

    private static boolean decodePhaseLoggingEnabled() {
        return Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty("vlm.benchmark.decodePhaseLogging", "true"));
    }

    private static boolean detailedDecodeDiagnosticsEnabled() {
        return Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty("vlm.benchmark.decodeDiagnostics", "false"))
                || Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty("vlm.benchmark.logitFingerprints", "false"))
                || Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty("vlm.benchmark.tensorFingerprints", "false"));
    }

    private static int diagnosticSteps() {
        return Integer.getInteger("vlm.benchmark.diagnosticSteps", DEFAULT_DIAGNOSTIC_STEPS);
    }

    /**
     * Reuses the token_sample op and output buffer across decode steps.
     * The per-step host readback still exists, but this removes the repeated
     * DynamicCustomOp construction and output allocation from the hot path.
     */
    private static final class ReusableTokenSampler {
        private final SamplingConfig samplingConfig;
        private TokenSample tokenSampleOp;
        private INDArray tokenOutput;
        private long outputBatchSize = -1;

        private ReusableTokenSampler(SamplingConfig samplingConfig) {
            this.samplingConfig = samplingConfig;
        }

        int sample(INDArray logits) {
            long batchSize = logits.rank() == 3 ? logits.size(0)
                    : (logits.rank() == 2 ? logits.size(0) : 1);

            if (tokenOutput == null || outputBatchSize != batchSize || tokenOutput.wasClosed()) {
                if (tokenOutput != null && !tokenOutput.wasClosed()) {
                    tokenOutput.setCloseable(true);
                    tokenOutput.close();
                }
                tokenOutput = Nd4j.createUninitialized(DataType.INT64, batchSize);
                outputBatchSize = batchSize;
            }

            if (tokenSampleOp == null) {
                if (samplingConfig.isGreedy()) {
                    tokenSampleOp = new TokenSample(logits);
                } else {
                    tokenSampleOp = new TokenSample(logits,
                            samplingConfig.getTemperature(),
                            samplingConfig.getTopK(),
                            samplingConfig.getTopP(),
                            samplingConfig.getSeed() != null ? samplingConfig.getSeed() : 0L);
                }
            } else {
                tokenSampleOp.setInputArgument(0, logits);
            }
            tokenSampleOp.setOutputArgument(0, tokenOutput);

            // Clear stale native error state from prior DSP graph-capture attempts.
            Nd4j.getNativeOps().clearLastError();
            Nd4j.getExecutioner().exec(tokenSampleOp);
            return tokenOutput.getInt(0);
        }

        void close() {
            if (tokenOutput != null && !tokenOutput.wasClosed()) {
                tokenOutput.setCloseable(true);
                tokenOutput.close();
            }

codex
I found a stronger native leak candidate than slot overwrites themselves: frozen execution pins every current output slot `DataBuffer` with `addFrozenRef()`, but the code I’ve seen only removes those refs from buffers that are still present in `outputSlots_` later. If any slot keeps getting replaced after freeze, `writeOutputSlot` can delete the old `NDArray` wrapper while the old `DataBuffer` remains artificially pinned and never actually frees. I’m verifying that path now.

codex
Another native ownership bucket is `Context::_intermediateResults`: unlike fastpath inputs/outputs, those are heap-owned by the `Context` and only freed in the `Context` destructor. Because DSP reuses one `Context` per slot for the life of the plan, any op that appends inference-time intermediates there would leak across decode steps. I’m checking whether that path is active in slot execution.

    37	/**
    38	 * Static (dense) KV cache manager for CUDA graph-compatible decode.
    39	 *
    40	 * <p>Pre-allocates dense [batch, heads, maxKvLen, headDim] buffers at prefill time
    41	 * and uses the native {@code kv_scatter} op (via {@link DecoderUtils#scatterNewKvEntries})
    42	 * to write new entries at each decode step. The buffers have fixed shapes after
    43	 * initialization, enabling CUDA graph capture and replay.</p>
    44	 *
    45	 * <h3>Scatter modes</h3>
    46	 * <ul>
    47	 *   <li><b>Java scatter</b> (default): Decoder outputs present KV tensors, Java calls
    48	 *       the batched KvScatter op to copy entries into static buffers.</li>
    49	 *   <li><b>C++ scatter</b>: When DSP's {@code configureKvCacheRetention} succeeds,
    50	 *       the native plan handles KV scatter internally and only outputs logits.
    51	 *       Controlled via the {@code kvScatterInCpp} flag.</li>
    52	 * </ul>
    53	 *
    54	 * <h3>Input modes</h3>
    55	 * <ul>
    56	 *   <li><b>Padded mode</b> (DSP active): Full static buffer passed as input with
    57	 *       sparse attention mask. Fixed shapes for CUDA graphs.</li>
    58	 *   <li><b>View mode</b> (no DSP): KV views [0:cachePos] passed as input with
    59	 *       all-ones attention mask. Growing shapes, no CUDA graph support.</li>
    60	 * </ul>
    61	 *
    62	 * @see KvCacheManager
    63	 * @see DecoderUtils#padKvCacheToStaticSize
    64	 * @see DecoderUtils#scatterNewKvEntries
    65	 */

    67	public class StaticKvCacheManager implements KvCacheManager {

   115	    public void initializeFromPrefill(Map<String, INDArray> prefillOutputs,
   116	                                      DecoderUtils.KVCacheNames kvNames,

   118	        this.maxKvLen = prefillSeqLen + maxNewTokens;

   120	                prefillSeqLen, maxKvLen, kvNames.keyNames.size(), kvNames.valueNames.size());

   122	        this.staticKvBuffers = DecoderUtils.padKvCacheToStaticSize(

   130	    @Override
   131	    public void initializeEmpty(SameDiff decoder, List<String> decoderInputNames,
   132	                                int maxKvLen, long hiddenSize) {
   133	        this.maxKvLen = maxKvLen;
   134	        this.staticKvBuffers = new HashMap<>();
   135	
   136	        List<String> pastInputNames = new ArrayList<>();
   137	        for (String inputName : decoderInputNames) {
   138	            if (ioConfig.isKvCacheInput(inputName)) {
   139	                pastInputNames.add(inputName);
   140	            }
   141	        }
   142	
   143	        for (String pastInputName : pastInputNames) {
   144	            INDArray empty = DecoderUtils.createEmptyKvCache(decoder, pastInputName, 1, hiddenSize);
   145	            long numHeads = empty.size(1);
   146	            long headDim = empty.size(3);
   147	            DataType kvType = empty.dataType();
   148	            empty.close();
   149	
   150	            INDArray buf = Nd4j.zeros(kvType, 1, numHeads, maxKvLen, headDim);
   151	            buf.setCloseable(false);
   152	            staticKvBuffers.put(pastInputName, buf);
   153	        }
   154	
   155	        this.cachePosition = 0;
   156	        this.initialized = true;
   157	        log.info("  StaticKvCacheManager: initialized empty with maxKvLen={}, {} buffers",
   158	                maxKvLen, staticKvBuffers.size());
   159	    }

   162	    public void prepareInputs(Map<String, INDArray> decoderInputMap, SameDiff decoder,
   163	                              long hiddenSize, boolean dspActive) {
   164	        if (!initialized || staticKvBuffers == null) return;
   165	
   166	        for (String inputName : decoder.inputs()) {
   167	            if (!ioConfig.isKvCacheInput(inputName)) continue;
   168	
   169	            INDArray staticBuf = staticKvBuffers.get(inputName);
   170	            if (staticBuf != null) {
   171	                if (dspActive) {
   172	                    // Padded mode: pass full static buffer (fixed shape for CUDA graphs)
   173	                    decoderInputMap.put(inputName, staticBuf);
   174	                } else {
   175	                    // View mode: pass VIEW [0:cachePos] (growing shapes)
   176	                    if (cachePosition > 0 && cachePosition < staticBuf.size(2)) {
   177	                        INDArray view = staticBuf.get(
   178	                                NDArrayIndex.all(), NDArrayIndex.all(),
   179	                                NDArrayIndex.interval(0, cachePosition), NDArrayIndex.all());
   180	                        decoderInputMap.put(inputName, view);
   181	                    } else if (cachePosition >= staticBuf.size(2)) {
   182	                        decoderInputMap.put(inputName, staticBuf);
   183	                    } else {
   184	                        decoderInputMap.put(inputName,
   185	                                DecoderUtils.createEmptyKvCache(decoder, inputName, 1, hiddenSize));
   186	                    }
   187	                }
   188	            } else {
   189	                decoderInputMap.put(inputName,
   190	                        DecoderUtils.createEmptyKvCache(decoder, inputName, 1, hiddenSize));
   191	            }
   192	        }
   193	    }
   194	
   195	    @Override
   196	    public void scatterNewEntries(Map<String, INDArray> decoderOutputs,
   197	                                  DecoderUtils.KVCacheNames kvNames) {
   198	        if (kvScatterInCpp) {
   199	            // C++ handles scatter internally -- just advance position
   200	            cachePosition++;
   201	            return;
   202	        }
   203	
   204	        // Java scatter via batched native KvScatter op
   205	        DecoderUtils.scatterNewKvEntries(staticKvBuffers, decoderOutputs,
   206	                kvNames.keyNames, kvNames.valueNames, maxKvLen, cachePosition);
   207	        cachePosition++;
   208	    }
   209	
   210	    @Override
   211	    public void scatterMultipleEntries(Map<String, INDArray> decoderOutputs,
   212	                                       DecoderUtils.KVCacheNames kvNames,
   213	                                       int numEntries) {
   214	        if (numEntries <= 0) return;
   215	
   216	        DecoderUtils.scatterMultipleKvEntries(staticKvBuffers, decoderOutputs,
   217	                kvNames.keyNames, kvNames.valueNames, maxKvLen, cachePosition, numEntries);
   218	        cachePosition += numEntries;
   219	    }
   220	
   221	    @Override
   222	    public void setCachePosition(long position) {
   223	        this.cachePosition = position;
   224	    }
   225	
   226	    @Override
   227	    public boolean isInitialized() {
   228	        return initialized;
   229	    }
   230	
   231	    @Override
   232	    public boolean supportsCudaGraphReplay() {
   233	        return true;
   234	    }
   235	
   236	    @Override
   237	    public Map<String, INDArray> getStaticKvBuffers() {
   238	        return staticKvBuffers;
   239	    }
   240	
   241	    @Override
   242	    public void close() {
   243	        if (staticKvBuffers != null) {
   244	            for (INDArray buf : staticKvBuffers.values()) {
   245	                if (buf != null && !buf.wasClosed()) {
   246	                    buf.setCloseable(true);
   247	                    buf.close();
   248	                }
   249	            }
   250	            staticKvBuffers = null;
   251	        }
   252	        initialized = false;
   253	        log.info("StaticKvCacheManager closed");
   254	    }
   255	}

codex
The static KV buffer path is subtler than I first thought. Empty-init buffers inherit the decoder input placeholder dtype, but prefill-padded buffers inherit the prefill output dtype. I’m checking that path because a dtype mismatch there would still create a full-cache cast on every decode step.

I do not see evidence that the 256 MB/step leak is coming from slot-resident DSP outputs. The native slot allocation/free path is present and internally consistent. The one concrete missing cleanup I found is outside `writeOutputSlot()`, in Java placeholder casting.

1. Exact allocation path for DSP outputs:
   `[InferenceSession.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/nd4j-backends/nd4j-api-parent/nd4j-api/src/main/java/org/nd4j/autodiff/samediff/internal/InferenceSession.java:862)` `862-928` enters the DSP fast path, and `1213-1274` calls the executor. The actual executor class is `[DynamicShapePlanExecutor.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/nd4j-backends/nd4j-api-parent/nd4j-api/src/main/java/org/nd4j/autodiff/samediff/execution/DynamicShapePlanExecutor.java:1353)` `1353-1372`, which always dispatches to native `executeNative()`.
   In `executeNative()` `2581-2587`, Java calls `nativeOps.executeDynamicShapePlan(...)`. Native then runs `[NativeDynamicShapePlan_segments.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/graph/impl/NativeDynamicShapePlan_segments.cpp:795)` `795-930`, which calls per-slot execution in `[NativeDynamicShapePlan_slotexec.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/graph/impl/NativeDynamicShapePlan_slotexec.cpp:1885)` `1885-2235`.
   The real output `NDArray` allocations happen there in Step 3: `1918-1931`, `2053-2055`, `2083-2086`, `2131-2134`, `2171-2197`, `2210-2235`. After allocation, the pointers are only bound into the per-slot `Context` at `2275-2284`; the `Context` is not allocating them.
   The plan returns requested outputs by aliasing `outputSlots_[slotIdx]` in `[NativeDynamicShapePlan.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/graph/impl/NativeDynamicShapePlan.cpp:1317)` `1317-1325` and `1958-1966`. JNI writes those same pointers back to the graph context in `libnd4j/include/legacy/cuda/NativeOps_dsp.cu:298-301`. Java then copies only requested outputs in `DynamicShapePlanExecutor.java:2616-2760`. With `[StaticKvCacheDecodeLoop.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/samediff-llm/src/main/java/org/eclipse/deeplearning4j/llm/generation/StaticKvCacheDecodeLoop.java:449)` `449-455`, `kvScatterInCpp` requests logits only, so Java-side output allocation is just logits.

2. Where these arrays should be freed:
   Slot-owned outputs should be freed on overwrite in `[NativeDynamicShapePlan.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/graph/impl/NativeDynamicShapePlan.cpp:253)` `306-331`, or at plan destruction in the same file `399-418`.
   `Context::setOutputArray()` in `[Context.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/graph/impl/Context.cpp:738)` `738-793` is non-owning unless `removable=true`. DSP slot execution uses the default `false` at `NativeDynamicShapePlan_slotexec.cpp:2283`.
   The concrete missing free I found is in `[InferenceSession.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/nd4j-backends/nd4j-api-parent/nd4j-api/src/main/java/org/nd4j/autodiff/samediff/internal/InferenceSession.java:3938)` `3938-3952`: `castPlaceholderTypes()` allocates cast copies with `castTo()`. The DSP-null path closes them at `877-891`, but the DSP-success path returns at `893-928` without closing them, and the exception path also lacks that cleanup.

3. Why `writeOutputSlot()` does not prevent the leak:
   It is being called for slot outputs. All normal slot allocation sites feed into it, and fused/view paths also end up there.
   Its free condition only skips deletion when `old == value`, when the old pointer is still referenced by another slot, or when the array is not in `planOwnedArrays_`. Those are alias/reuse cases, not “fresh 256 MB buffer every step” cases.
   So if the leak is real and linear per step, the stronger code fit is “allocation outside `outputSlots_` ownership,” not a missing delete inside `writeOutputSlot()`.

4. `OpContext::purge()` / `setOutputArray()`:
   `Context::clearFastPath()` in `[Context.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/graph/impl/Context.cpp:986)` `986-1013` only clears fastpath vectors; it explicitly does not delete `_handles`.
   There is a real latent leak bucket in `Context::~Context()` `209-216`: `_handles` are cleared, not deleted. That ownership path is created by `[DeclarableOp.cpp](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/libnd4j/include/ops/declarable/impl/DeclarableOp.cpp:409)` `524-527` via `ctx.setOutputArray(idx, outArr, true)`.
   But the normal DSP slot path bypasses that: slot executor prebinds outputs and sets `ctx.setShapeFunctionOverride(true)` at `NativeDynamicShapePlan_slotexec.cpp:2295`, and `DeclarableOp::prepareOutputs()` returns early at `DeclarableOp.cpp:409-412`. So `_handles` is not the normal steady-state decode path.
   `_intermediateResults` are also persistent in pooled native `Context`s, but I only found producers in conv2d helpers, not transformer decode.

5. Per-step arrays created in the DSP path that are not freed:
   Proven candidate: the placeholder cast copies in `InferenceSession.castPlaceholderTypes()`.
   There are also tiny dummy output placeholders in `DynamicShapePlanExecutor.java:2487-2492`, but those are `Nd4j.empty(DataType.FLOAT)` and not a 256 MB source.
   The external-buffer wrappers created during output copy are deleted correctly in `executeNative()` at `2654-2664` and `2700-2710`.
   The standard `executeOperations()` path is not involved when DSP succeeds; `InferenceSession.output()` returns from the DSP branch before `941-960`.

Most likely root cause from code inspection:
`writeOutputSlot()` is probably not the leak. The strongest concrete leak path is the missing cleanup of DSP placeholder cast copies in `InferenceSession`. That becomes a full-cache leak if any decode placeholder is cast every step. This is especially plausible for static KV after prefill, because `[DecoderUtils.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/samediff-llm/src/main/java/org/eclipse/deeplearning4j/llm/generation/DecoderUtils.java:304)` `304-345` pads static KV buffers using `prefillKv.dataType()`, while empty-init KV buffers use the decoder input placeholder dtype at `138-186`, and `[StaticKvCacheManager.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/samediff-llm/src/main/java/org/eclipse/deeplearning4j/llm/generation/StaticKvCacheManager.java:143)` `143-173` passes those static buffers back into DSP every step.

What I can prove from code:
- native slot outputs are allocated in the C++ slot cache and have an overwrite/destructor free path
- `Context::purge()` is not the main DSP output owner
- Java DSP placeholder casts have a missing cleanup path

What I cannot prove from code alone:
- whether SmolDocling’s actual `past_key_values.*` placeholders and static KV buffers differ in dtype at runtime. If they do, that missing cleanup exactly matches the symptom.

   Proven candidate: the placeholder cast copies in `InferenceSession.castPlaceholderTypes()`.
   There are also tiny dummy output placeholders in `DynamicShapePlanExecutor.java:2487-2492`, but those are `Nd4j.empty(DataType.FLOAT)` and not a 256 MB source.
   The external-buffer wrappers created during output copy are deleted correctly in `executeNative()` at `2654-2664` and `2700-2710`.
   The standard `executeOperations()` path is not involved when DSP succeeds; `InferenceSession.output()` returns from the DSP branch before `941-960`.

Most likely root cause from code inspection:
`writeOutputSlot()` is probably not the leak. The strongest concrete leak path is the missing cleanup of DSP placeholder cast copies in `InferenceSession`. That becomes a full-cache leak if any decode placeholder is cast every step. This is especially plausible for static KV after prefill, because `[DecoderUtils.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/samediff-llm/src/main/java/org/eclipse/deeplearning4j/llm/generation/DecoderUtils.java:304)` `304-345` pads static KV buffers using `prefillKv.dataType()`, while empty-init KV buffers use the decoder input placeholder dtype at `138-186`, and `[StaticKvCacheManager.java](/home/agibsonccc/Documents/GitHub/deeplearning4j/nd4j/samediff-llm/src/main/java/org/eclipse/deeplearning4j/llm/generation/StaticKvCacheManager.java:143)` `143-173` passes those static buffers back into DSP every step.

What I can prove from code:
- native slot outputs are allocated in the C++ slot cache and have an overwrite/destructor free path
- `Context::purge()` is not the main DSP output owner
- Java DSP placeholder casts have a missing cleanup path

What I cannot prove from code alone:
- whether SmolDocling’s actual `past_key_values.*` placeholders and static KV buffers differ in dtype at runtime. If they do, that missing cleanup exactly matches the symptom.
